tool_summary: Attaches a filesystem, device, or network share to a directory in the filesystem tree.
platform_notes: Core invocation and effect are consistent across GNU/Linux and BSD/macOS mount; specific filesystem type support and option names vary but that detail is out of scope for this baseline ruleset.

rules.description: Bind mounts (--bind) and remote filesystem mounts (nfs, cifs, sshfs) expose one part of the filesystem inside another location, or attach network-controlled storage, either of which can be used to bypass path-based access assumptions elsewhere in the system.
rules.reversible_note: The mount can be undone with umount, but data written or read while mounted is not.

rules.description: Attaches a filesystem or device to the filesystem tree. Typically requires root privileges, and changes what storage is accessible at a given path.
rules.reversible_note: The mount can be undone with umount, but data written while mounted is not.
